Messages.Author: bobby_doc
Messages.Body:
Just make alternative tournaments with restricted decks.

How should they be restricted?
Here’s some suggestions (maybe you guys got other ideas), use one or
more:
1. Max deck size

2. Restrict or ban specific cards

3. Card limit á la Magic (yack!)
4. Minimum crypt average
5. Maximum crypt size
6. Give decks with higher crypt average an advantage when comparing with
decks with lower crypt average which have the same amount vp.
7. Make two lists(some chosen good cards on one list and some chosen
bad cards on the other) – if a deck contains a certain amount of cards
from the good list that deck gets penalties of some kind and vice versa.

8. In each tournament round your prey may name three(less?more?) cards
the predator may not play. Each time the predator gets one of these
cards, he/she immediatly discards it and draws a new one.

I know. Some of these maybe aren't so good.
But we have to discuss this, right?

If some of this kind of tournaments gets popular, we'll get much
"funnier" decks floating around.

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
bobby_doc wrote:
>>1. Max deck size>>

DCI rules already say minimum 60/maximum 90 with a minimum 12 card crypt.

>>2. Restrict or ban specific cards>>

There are some banned cards (mostly ante cards, but a few are banned for play
balance reasons), and restricting cards goes against the very basis of the
game.

>>3. Card limit á la Magic (yack!)>>

Nah. This one never works. It makes certain perfectly reasonable decks
implayable (Rush decks, Eagle's Sight decks, Ani based intercept decks, etc),
and other perfectly reasonable decks way too powerful (Malk S+B) due to decks
that usually counter them being non playable. The end result is a different
environment with different decks being too good, which isn't any better, just
different.

>>4. Minimum crypt average>>

This one seems pretty reasonable for a variant tournament, but I really don't
think that it will work all that well, and won't really stop a weenie deck.
Assuming you wanted to enforce a average vampire size of 4, the weenie deck
could compose a crypt of:

3x IC members (33)
2x 3 point vamps (6)
2x 2 point vamps (4)
5x 1 point vamps (5)

Or some such variation, giving him 9 weenie vampires to work with and 3 IC
members to never influence out. Between the countless Effective Managements and
Info Highways, the 3 IC members included will have a negligible effect on their
strategy.

>>5. Maximum crypt size>>

Not really an issue. 12 vampires is ussually sufficient for a given deck.

>>6. Give decks with higher crypt average an advantage when comparing with
decks with lower crypt average which have the same amount vp.>>

Again, suffers from the averaging problem. What kind of advantage would you
give them?

>>7. Make two lists(some chosen good cards on one list and some chosen

bad cards on the other) ˆ if a deck contains a certain amount of cards

from the good list that deck gets penalties of some kind and vice versa.>>

Hmm. A bit arbitrary, and makes it really easy to screw over your prey by
scouting out their deck.

>>8. In each tournament round your prey may name three(less?more?) cards
the predator may not play. Each time the predator gets one of these
cards, he/she immediatly discards it and draws a new one.>>

This one is just insane. It's kinda funny, sure, but really not a good idea. By

allowing somone to surgically remove certain cards from an opponents deck, they
can make their decks invulnerable ("Hmm. You are a Rush deck. You may not play
with Bum's Rush, Haven Uncovered, and Immortal Grapple." "Doh." or "Hmm. You
are an intercept deck. You may not play with Wake, Enhanced Senses, or Eagle's
Sight." "Doh".) However, as they also have cards surgically removed from their
decks, their decks become unworkable. In the end, you have a whole table of
people playing Werewolf Pack decks and getting nowhere. Funny idea, though :-)

Peter D Bakija

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
Robert Doktorow wrote:
>>Yeah, I know this will kill decks that depends on a few specific cards.
That's the point. It will force the players to design more allround
decks. Horrible, isn't it ;-) You can restict this a little, you can name any
three cards EXCEPT blooddoll and wake (others?)>>

This runs into the same problems as a blanket card limit--it completely hobbles
decks that rely on cards that don't have much in the way of redundancy, yet
hardly affects decks that use cards of which there are countless variations.

For instance, take a plain, brown, old fashion Malk Stealth and Bleed deck.
Just looking at Obf cards that provide stealth, we have:

Lost in Crowds
Faceless Night
Cloak the Gathering
Mask of 1000K
Scouting Mission
Swallowed by Night
Elder Impersonation

Looking at Dom bleed cards, we have:

Bonding
Threats
Conditioning
Forshadowing Destruction
Command the Beast
Govern the Unaligned
Scouting Mission
Dominate Kine

I'm sure there are others that I'm forgetting. Anyway, as a result of there
being so many "duplicate" cards, that while all subtley different, all pretty
much do the same thing. If, given the idea of being able to remove 2 or 3 of a
particular card from your prey's deck, how does this harm such a Malk S+B deck?
It won't at all. If he uses 3 of each of 8 cards, rather than 24 of 1 card, his
deck will still work more or less the same, and will be completely unaffected
by the variant rule.

On the other hand, you have decks that revolve around one particular card that
there is no duplication of in the set--Rush decks that use Immortal Grapple;
Intercept decks that use Eagle's Sight; Celerity decks that use Alacrity. In
such a situation, where specific cards are removed (or restricted to 4 of
each), these decks cease to function, where simillarly focused decks that use
cards that have a great deal of redundancy (like S+B decks) are completely
unaffected.

What this would result in is a different environment where different decks are
too good--most people who play 4CL call Malk S+B decks "cheesy", because they
are too good in that environment (which they are).

>

All cards are to be played according to their latest printings [DCI 2.1.1]
(with errata, of course).

The latest printing of Gangrel De-evolution is Gangrel Atavism. So
Gangrel De-evoilution is to be played as if it read the same way as
Gangrel Atavism.

Similarly, the latest printing of Stake is Wooden Stake, so it is
to be played the same as Wooden Stake.

Etc.

The changes were listed in an article in the Duelist #7. You can tell

that they are the same card by the artwork (which remained the same
through the renaming process). They are:

Stake bacame Wooden Stake (and was rewritten).
Gangrel De-Evolution became Gangel Atavism (and was reworded).
Kine Dominance became Dominate Kine (and was reworded).>

The other changes (not listed in that article) are obvious.

For instance, you couldn't play an Eco Terrorists and an
Ecoterrorists without contesting them - they are obviously the same
card. And a single vampire couldn't play both Spirit's Touch and The

Spirit's Touch on the same action. Etc.
